 In The Court Of Ms. Vrinda Kumari
 Presiding Officer:Motor Accident Claims
 Tribunal Patiala House Courts, New Delhi
 In The Matter Of:
 Hrithik Vs. Harish Chander Bisht & Ors.

1. Ramu @ Rhitik @ Hritik  Aged about 19 years old  S/o Sh. Mani Ram  R/o H.No. 205/115,

 S/o Sh. Naryan Singh Bisht  R/o 410, P&T Colony, Sector-6,

2. National Insurance Co.Ltd (Insurer)
 National Legal Vertical, 
 2 E/9, IInd Floor,
 Jhandewalan Extension,
 New Delhi - 110055.
 Vide Policy No. 35180031156100001215  Valid from 16.08.2015 to 15.08.2016. 
3. Sh. Surinder Singh Rawat (Registered owner)
 S/o Sh. Daljit Singh Rawat  R/o GH-14, H.No. 36, DDA Flats,
 Paschim Vihar, New Delhi-87. ....Respondents  Date of filing of DAR : 24.01.2017 Date of framing of issues : 30.05.2017 Date of concluding arguments : 12.07.2024 Date of decision : 20.07.2024 AWARD/JUDGMENT 1. The present DAR (Detailed Accident Report) for compensation relates to grievous injury suffered by the claimant Sh. Ramu @ Rhitik @ Hritik in a road accident that took place on 03.04.2016 at around 10 PM at near H. No. 758, Sector 6, R.K. Puram, New Delhi regarding which an FIR bearing No.244/16 under Sections 279/338 IPC was registered at PS RK Puram. The offending vehicle involved in this case is a car bearing registration no. DL-8CK-4477 which at the time of accident was Hrithik vs Harish Chander Bisht on 20 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138349291/
1 being driven by respondent No. 1 (R-1) Sh. Harish Chander, insured with respondent no. 2 (R-2)
National Insurance Company Ltd. and owned by respondent No. 3 (R-3) Sh. Surinder Singh Rawat.
2. Facts of the case as per DAR are that on the aforesaid date, time and place of accident, the claimant was coming back to his residence after attending a marriage party from Arya Samaj Mandir, Sector-6, RK Puram alongwith his two friends on a scooty bearing registration no.
DL-3SDD-4208 which was being driven by his friend. Claimant was the pillion rider. When they reached near H.No. 758, Sector-6, RK Puram, all of a sudden a Maruti 800 car bearing registration no. DL-8CK-4477 which was being driven by R-1 in a rash and negligent manner hit the said scooty due to which claimant fell down on the road and received grievous injuries. Claimant was taken to Jaiprakash Narayan Apex Trauma Centre, AIIMS.
3. In his Written Statement, R-1 controverted the allegations of the claimant. He has submitted that the accident was caused because of sole negligence on part of the injured/claimant who was the second pillion rider and was without helmet. The rider of the scooty was under the influence of liquor because of which they lost balance and fell down near the stationary vehicle/car of R1. It is submitted that R-1 had purchased the said car from R-3 Sh. Surender Singh Rawat on 02.03.2016. 
At the time of accident, he had parked the vehicle at the extreme left hand side of the road with parking indicators on. It was the scooty on which the claimant and his two friends were riding without helmet that lost control. It is submitted by the respondent that he also helped in carrying the injured in an auto to AIIMS Trauma Centre and also paid auto fare along with initial expenses of treatment in cash. 
4. In his WS, R-3/registered owner of the vehicle submitted that he had sold the offending car to R-1 on 02.03.2016 after executing all the required documents. The duly filled form no . 29 and 30 were handed over to R-1 alongwith original documents such as RC, Insurance, PUC and duplicate keys alongwith physical possession of the offending car. Subsequently, delivery receipt duly signed on Re.
1 Revenue Stamp by R-1 was handed over to R-3.
5. In its Written Statement, R-2/Insurance Company averred that the offending vehicle was insured with it vide a policy which was valid from 16.08.2015 to 15.08.2016. It was insured in the name of R-3 Sh. Surinder Singh Rawat. The offending vehicle was, however, transferred by R-3 to R-1 Sh.
Harish Chander Bisht before the accident without intimating the Insurance Company. It is submitted that driver of the offending vehicle was driving the said vehicle in contravention of various provisions of Motor Vehicle Act. He also did not hold proper and valid driving license. It has further been contended that the claimant was a pillion rider of the motorcycle bearing registration no. DL-3SDD-4208. This motorcycle was being driven without driving license and three persons were riding on it without helmet. It is submitted that as per the DAR there was a head on collision between the two vehicles. On these grounds, it has been contended that Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation. 
6. Vide Order dated 30.05.2017, following issues were framed:
Hrithik vs Harish Chander Bisht on 20 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138349291/
2 1. Whether Sh. Hritik sustained injuries in the accident which occurred on 03.04.2016 at about 10.00 PM near House no. 758, Sector-6, R.K. Puram, Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. Dl-8CK-4477 being driven and owned by respondent no. 1 and insured with respondent no. 2?OPP 2. Whether the claimant is entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. Relief.
7. On 23.02.2019, issues framed on 30.05.2017 were amended which are as follows :
1. Whether Sh. Hritik sustained grievous injuries in the accident which occurred on 03.04.2016 at about 10 PM near House No. 758, Sector-6, R.K. Puram, Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. DL-8CK-4477 alleged to be driven by respondent no. 1 and also alleged to be purchased and possessed by him, insured with respondent no. 2 and registered in the name of respondent no. 3? OPP 2. Whether the claimant is entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. Relief.
8. During the course of PE, claimant Sh. Ramu @ Rhitik @ Hrithik examined himself as PW1. His affidavit in evidence is Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon the certain documents. His discharge summary is Ex.PW1/1. OPD prescription slips are Ex.PW1/2 (Colly). Medical Bills are Ex.PW1/3 (Colly). DAR is Ex.PW1/4.
9. During RE, R-1 Sh. Harish Chander Bisht examined himself as R1W1. His affidavit in evidence is Ex.R1W1/A. He relied upon certain documents. The discharge slip dated 12.04.2016 and prescription slip dated 01.05.2017 are Ex.R1W1/1 (colly) (OSR). Copy of medical bill dated 04.04.2016 is Ex.R1W1/2 (OSR).
10. R-2 Insurance Company examined Sh. Vineet Kumar, Assistant/AR of Insurance Company as R2W1. His affidavit in evidence is Ex.R2W1/A. He relied upon certain documents. Attested copy of insurance policy is Ex.R2W1/1. Copies of notice under Order 12 Rule 8 CPC given to the driver cum owner as well as to the registered owner alongwith postal receipts are Ex.R2W1/2 to Ex.R2W1/4 respectively. 
11. Financial Statement of the claimant was recorded on 09.02.2024. He stated that at the time of accident, he was unemployed and was now doing a private job and earning around 10,000/- per month. He was unmarried. He had suffered 2% permanent disability due to injuries sustained in the accident. He stated that his household expenses were around Rs. 15,000/- to Rs. 20,000/- per month. 
Hrithik vs Harish Chander Bisht on 20 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138349291/
3 12. The Tribunal heard the final arguments advanced by Sh. Amit Ranjan, Ld. Counsel for claimant,
Sh. Prem Kumar, Ld. Counsel for R-1, Ms. Geeta Malhotra, Ld. Counsel for R-2/Insurance Company and Sh. Abhishek Raina, Ld. Counsel for R-3. The Tribunal has carefully perused the entire case record along with written submissions. The findings on the aforementioned issues are rendered hereinafter in the succeeding paragraphs. 
1. 1. Whether Sh. Hritik sustained grievous injuries in the accident which occurred on 03.04.2016 at about 10 PM near House No. 758, Sector-6, R.K. Puram, Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. DL-8CK-4477 alleged to be driven by respondent no. 1 and also alleged to be purchased and possessed by him, insured with respondent no. 2 and registered in the name of respondent no. 3? OPP 13. Onus to prove this issue was upon the claimant. The first question that needs to be decided is whether the accident was caused by the vehicle bearing registration No. HR-55-S-1417.
14. PW1/claimant has deposed in his affidavit in evidence regarding the circumstances in which accident took place. He has deposed as follows:
"2. That I say that on the unfortunate day of 03.04.2016 I was coming back to my residence after attending my friend marriage party from Arya Samaj Mandir,
Sector-6, R.K. Puram, Delhi. My friend who was riding on a scooty bearing registration no. DL-3SDD-4208 met me on the way and I requested him for lift for going to Main Road. I seated on the said scooty as a pillion rider and I along with my friend on the said scooty was going to the Main Road through the Service Road. The said scooty was being driven by my friend with due care caution by observing traffic rules and regulations and by observing proper look out on his proper side. At about 09:40 P.M., when I reached near H. NO. 758, Sector-6, R.K. Puram, New Delhi, at the same time all of sudden an offending Maruti 800 car in white colour Car bearing registration no.
DL-8CK-4477 which was being driven by its driver in a rash, negligent and reckless manner, by violating traffic rules and regulations, by not observing proper look out and at a break-neck speed came from the wrong side and hit my said scooty with violent force. Due to the heavy impact I along with my friend and scooty fell down on the road and I received serious/ grievous injuries all over my body. The accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving on the part of respondent no. 1. the driver of the offending vehicle. " 
15. During his cross examination, PW1 admitted that he was riding the scooty along with his two friends. He has further deposed that they all were wearing helmets. He was not aware if his friend Amit who was driving the scooty was holding a driving license at the time of accident or not. 
16. R1W1 Harish Chander Bisht (driver of the offending vehicle) entered the witness box and he deposed during his cross examination by Ld. Counsel for the Insurance Company that none of the Hrithik vs Harish Chander Bisht on 20 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138349291/
4 three boys on scooty were wearing helmet. Chargesheet is silent on this aspect. I will, therefore,
consider the statement of the claimant/injured on the basis of which the FIR in the present case was registered. In this statement, the claimant/injured stated that he was returning home from Arya Samaj Temple after attending a marriage ceremony when he spotted his two friends coming on a scooty. He requested a lift to his home from his friends which request was acceded to by them. In such a circumstance, it is improbable that the claimant was riding the scooty with helmet on. 
17. Even though, it is probable that the claimant was riding the scooty without helmet, it was not a factor which contributed to occurrence of the said accident. No doubt, not wearing a helmet at the time of riding a two wheeler amounts to violation of law/rules, it does not fall within the ambit of contributory negligence. 
18. Similarly, even though triple riding on scooty is a violation of law/rules for which penal action could be taken against such riders, there is nothing to show that such triple riding led to the accident in question. In Mohammed Siddique & Anr. Vs. National Insurance Company Ltd. & Ors. AIR 2020 SUPREME COURT 520, it has been held as follows:
"13. But the above reason, in our view, is flawed. The fact that the deceased was riding on a motor cycle along with the driver and another, may not, by itself, without anything more, make him guilty of contributory negligence. At the most it would make him guilty of being a party to the violation of the law. Section 128 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, imposes a restriction on the driver of a two- wheeled motor cycle,
not to carry more than one person on the motor cycle. Section 194 C inserted by the Amendment Act 32 of 2019, prescribes a penalty for violation of safety measures for motor cycle drivers and pillion riders. Therefore, the fact that a person was a pillion rider on a motor cycle along with the driver and one more person on the pillion, may be a violation of the law. But such violation by itself, without anything more, cannot lead to a finding of contributory negligence, unless it is established that his very act of riding along with two others, contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim. There must either be a causal connection between the violation and the accident or a causal connection between the violation and the impact of the accident upon the victim. It may so happen at times, that the accident could have been averted or the injuries sustained could have been of a lesser degree,
if there had been no violation of the law by the victim. What could otherwise have resulted in a simple injury, might have resulted in a grievous injury or even death due to the violation of the law by the victim. It is in such cases, where, but for the violation of the law, either the accident could have been averted or the impact could have been minimized, that the principle of contributory negligence could be invoked. 
It is not the case of the insurer that the accident itself occurred as a result of three persons riding on a motor cycle. It is not even the case of the insurer that the accident would have been averted, if three persons were not riding on the motor cycle. The fact that the motor cycle was hit by the car from behind, is admitted. Interestingly, the finding recorded by the Tribunal that the deceased was wearing a helmet and that the deceased was knocked down after the car hit the motor cycle from behind, are all not Hrithik vs Harish Chander Bisht on 20 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138349291/
5 assailed. Therefore, the finding of the High Court that 2 persons on the pillion of the motor cycle, could have added to the imbalance, is nothing but presumptuous and is not based either upon pleading or upon the evidence on record. Nothing was extracted from PW-3 to the effect that 2 persons on the pillion added to the imbalance. 
14. Therefore, in the absence of any evidence to show that the wrongful act on the part of the deceased victim contributed either to the accident or to the nature of the injuries sustained, the victim could not have been held guilty of contributory negligence. 
Hence the reduction of 10% towards contributory negligence, is clearly unjustified and the same has to be set aside." 
19. Coming to the next limb of argument, the Court agrees with the contention of the Insurance Company that in a case of head on collision between two vehicles, like in present case, 50% contributory negligence is attributable to both the vehicles. The Tribunal, however, is of the view that such 50% contributory negligence could have been attributed to the person driving the scooty. It can not be attributed to the pillion rider. 
20. As per the chargesheet, the accident in question took place because of rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle i.e. Maruti 800 car bearing registration no.
DL-8CK-4477 by R-1.
21. In cases National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287 and United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Deepak Goel and Ors., 2014 (2) TAC 846 (Del.)
decided by the Coordinate Bench of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court, it was held that "......where the claimants filed either the certified copies of the criminal record or the criminal record showing the completion of investigation by police or issuance of charge sheet under Section 279/304A IPC or the certified copy of FIR or the recovery of the mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle, then these documents are sufficient proof to reach to a conclusion that the driver was negligent particularly when there is no defence available from the side of driver."
22. Reliance is being placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Meera Devi & ors., 2021 LawSuit (Del) 2021 wherein it was held that "......in view of Delhi Motor Accident Claim Tribunal Rules, 2008, contents of DAR has to be presumed to be correct and read in evidence without formal proof of the same unless proof to the contrary was produced."
23. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303 has observed that filing of charge sheet against the driver prima facie points towards his complicity in driving the vehicle rashly and negligently. It has been further observed that even when Hrithik vs Harish Chander Bisht on 20 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138349291/
6 the accused were to be acquitted in the criminal case, the same may be of no effect on the assessment of the liability required in respect of motor accident cases by the Tribunal. 
24. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in Civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution. Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others , 
wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants and the claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
25. In his evidence, R1W1 (Respondent no.1 driver) deposed that because of a fault in his car, he had parked it at the extreme left hand side of the road by switching on its parking indicator lights. He had hardly checked his car for about two to three minutes when he heard loud sound of horns of the car passing by his car from the opposite direction. When he tried to find out if he had caused any traffic jam, he saw a scooty on which three boys including the claimant were riding coming towards him in a rash and negligent manner. The scooty tried to over take the car ahead of it but lost its balance and fell down just near his stationary car. The testimony of this witness would show that he has tried to create a case that no collision between his car and scooty took place. During the course of arguments, it was submitted on behalf of R-1 that mechanical inspection report would show that his car did not suffer any damage. In light of this argument, it would be apt to refer to his cross examination wherein he admitted that the offending vehicle was seized after eight to nine months from the date of accident. The Court agrees with the contention of Ld. Counsel for the claimant that the probability of getting the car repaired during this period of eight to nine months was very high. 
Further, there is nothing on record which would corroborate the version of R-1.
26. R-1 and R-2 could not bring any material on record to show that the conclusion of the IO in the case FIR No. 244/16 PS R.K. Puram to the effect that the accident was caused on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by R-1 was an erroneous conclusion. The testimony of PW1 is well corroborated by the chargesheet in the said FIR. 
27. In view of foregoing discussion, it stands proved by preponderance of probability that the aforesaid accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle i.e. Maruti 800 car bearing registration no. DL-8CK-4477 and that the said vehicle at that time was being driven by R-1, owned by R-3 and insured with R-2. Hence, this issue is decided in favour of the claimants and against the respondents. 
ISSUE NO.2 2. Whether the injured is entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
28 . As the issue No.1 has been proved in favour of the claimant, he has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered by him in the accident, but the computation of compensation Hrithik vs Harish Chander Bisht on 20 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138349291/
7 and liability to pay the same are required to be decided. 
29. In terms of Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, the compensation which is to be awarded by this Tribunal is required to be 'just'. In injury cases, a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343, has laid down heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases as:-
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses. 
Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages) 
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. 
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). 
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
30. Having considered the ratio of aforesaid judgment, the compensation payable to claimant is assessed hereinafter under the following heads as:-
(i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 31. In his affidavit Ex. PW1/A, the claimant has tendered on record his discharge summary Ex.
PW1/2, as per which the claimant was admitted in JPNA Trauma Centre on 03.04.2016 and was transferred to another hospital on 04.04.2016. As per discharge summary Ex. PW1/1, the claimant was admitted in VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital, New Delhi on 13.04.2016 and was discharged on 21.04.2016 where he was diagnosed with closed traumatic fracture shaft of femur and had undergone open reduction and internal fixation of fracture shaft of femur right was done with interlocking nail. 
Hrithik vs Harish Chander Bisht on 20 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138349291/
8 32. The claimant in his affidavit Ex. PW1/A has tendered on record his original medical bills which are totalling to a sum of Rs.3,879/-. The respondents have failed to lead any evidence to show that the said medical bills do not relate to the injuries suffered by the claimant in the aforesaid accident. 
Thus, the testimony of PW-1 that he had spent the aforesaid amount towards medical expenses remained unrebutted and uncontroverted. In the absence of any plausible evidence produced by respondents on record, there is no reason to disbelieve the testimony of PW-1 that he had spent the aforesaid amount towards medical expenses. Hence, he is held entitled to Rs.3,879/- towards his medical expenses. 
(ii) Loss of earnings 33. Claimant in his affidavit Ex. PW1/A has claimed that at the time of accident, he was doing private job and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month. During cross examination, he deposed that at the time of accident, he was working with DJ Satish and getting around Rs. 500/- to Rs. 600/- per day but he did not have any document to show his appointment/employment with above DJ Satish. 
He admitted that he had neither placed on record his educational certificate nor had he done diploma or any other course with regard to any skilled work. 
34. Since the employment and educational qualifications of the claimant could not be established on record, the minimum wages of unskilled person is taken into account as per rates prevalent in Delhi,
which was Rs.9,568/- per month at the time of accident. 
35. Keeping in view the nature of injury suffered by the claimant as well as duration of his treatment, this tribunal finds it just and reasonable to compensate him for loss of earning equivalent to a period of three months. Therefore, under this head, he is being awarded an amount of Rs.
28,704/- (Rs.9,568/- X 3 months). 
(iii) Loss of future earnings 36. As per disability certificate issued by Dr. RML Hospital, the claimant is a case of road traffic accident with fracture of shaft of femur right side, fracture has been united and had suffered 2%
permanent physical disability in relation to right lower limb. 
37. The law with regard to grant of compensation due to permanent disability and determination of functional disability etc. was well settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs.
Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343, wherein it has been held as under :-
"4. The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. 
The court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the Hrithik vs Harish Chander Bisht on 20 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138349291/
9 nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. (See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D.
Hattangadi vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467).
10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps. The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent ability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life). The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age. The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood, or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood. For example, if the left hand of a claimant is amputated, the permanent physical or functional disablement may be assessed around 60%. If the claimant was a driver or a carpenter, the actual loss of earning capacity may virtually be hundred percent, if he is neither able to drive or do carpentry. On the other hand, if the claimant was a clerk in government service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be continued as a clerk as he could perform his clerical functions; and in that event the loss of earning capacity will not be 100% as in the case of a driver or carpenter, nor 60% which is the actual physical disability, but far less. In fact, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of `loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in government service,
though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities as a consequence of losing his hand. Sometimes the injured claimant may be continued in service, but may not found suitable for discharging the duties attached to the post or job which he was earlier holding, on account of his disability, and may therefore be shifted to some other suitable but lesser post with lesser emoluments, in which case there should be a limited award under the head of loss of future earning capacity,
taking note of the reduced earning capacity. It may be noted that when compensation is awarded by treating the loss of future earning capacity as 100% (or even anything more than 50%), the need to award compensation separately under the head of loss of amenities or loss of expectation of life may disappear and as a result, only a token or nominal amount may have to be awarded under the head of loss of amenities or loss of expectation of life, as otherwise there may be a duplication in the award of compensation. Be that as it may............." 
Hrithik vs Harish Chander Bisht on 20 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138349291/
10 38. The claimant in his affidavit Ex. PW1/A has deposed that on account of injuries received in the accident, he is unable to attend his job which requires more physical involvement and his right leg became very weak due to which he is unable to run, walk and move properly. 
39. Considering the legal position discussed above coupled with the testimony of claimant, the functional disability of claimant is taken as 2% in relation to whole body, i.e. equivalent to the disability mentioned in the disability certificate. 
40. To apply the multiplier, it is necessary to ascertain the age of the claimant. The claimant has mentioned the age of claimant as 19 years in the amended memo of parties filed on record. 
However, in the DAR filed by the IO, the age of claimant is mentioned as 18 years. Hence, the age of claimant is taken as around 18-19 years at the time of accident. Therefore, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in a judgment of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors., SLP (Civil)
No. 25590 of 2014 dated 31.10.2017, the multiplier of '18' is applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of the claimant arising out of above disability, which is also mentioned in the written submissions filed on behalf of claimant and Insurance Company.
41. Further, the claimant is also held entitled to 40% future prospects in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi & Ors.(Supra). Thus, the loss of future earnings caused to the claimant due to his permanent disability comes to Rs.57,867/- (rounded off) (Rs.9,568/- X 12 X 2/100 X 18 X 140/100). 
(iv) Mental and Physical Shock, Pain and Sufferings & Loss of Amenities 42. As stated above, the claimant had suffered grievous injuries in the accident. Though, it is not possible to exactly compensate him for the shock, pain and sufferings etc. which he had actually suffered because of the above injuries, but an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner. Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by the claimant and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.30,000/-
each is being awarded to him towards mental and physical shock & for pain and sufferings. Further,
an amount of Rs.15,000/- is also awarded to him towards the loss of amenities suffered by him during said period of his treatment. Thus, he is awarded total amount of Rs.75,000/- under this head. 
(v) Conveyance, Special Diet and Attendant Charges 43. Claimant in his affidavit Ex. PW1/A has claimed that he had incurred an amount of Rs.20,000/-
to Rs.25,000/- each on special diet for early recovery and conveyance. However, he has not placed on record any document in order to substantiate his above claims. Therefore, the fact that a person was a pillion rider on a motor cycle along with the driver and one more person on the pillion, may be a violation of the law.

But such violation by itself, without anything more, cannot lead to a finding of contributory negligence, unless it is established that his very act of riding along with two others, contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim.
There must either be a causal connection between the violation and the accident or a causal connection between the violation and the impact of the accident upon the victim.

It may so happen at times, that the accident could have been averted or the injuries sustained could have been of a lesser degree,

What could otherwise have resulted in a simple injury, might have resulted in a grievous injury or even death due to the violation of the law by the victim.

There must either be a causal connection between the violation and the accident or a causal connection between the violation and the impact of the accident upon the victim.
It may so happen at times, that the accident could have been averted or the injuries sustained could have been of a lesser degree,
if there had been no violation of the law by the victim.
What could otherwise have resulted in a simple injury, might have resulted in a grievous injury or even death due to the violation of the law by the victim.
It is in such cases, where, but for the violation of the law, either the accident could have been averted or the impact could have been minimized, that the principle of contributory negligence could be invoked.
